answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one season of supervised falconry fieldwork, logging every trained flight into a public raptor atlas that reviewers audit. A weekly pulse check-in pings each holder to appear live at the survey site within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two identities at once. Each season needs a licensed falconer mentor who takes at most two apprentices, and the permit fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail. Every extra fake costs another bird, another season of fieldwork, another mentor slot, and twice the prior fee.
